feature1.prompt: An identity matrix is generated by computing M.T * M under the assumption that M is orthogonal. In such cases the matrix is recognized correctly as an identity matrix – its elements, when inspected individually and along the diagonal, yield the expected results. This indicates that the per‐element evaluation and the diagonal summation are functioning as intended, reflecting the standard properties of an identity matrix. The task is to review and improve the internal computation logic to ensure that the individual element assignments are robust and maintainable.
feature1.hint_texts: Modify the _entry method in sympy/matrices/expressions/matexpr.py to replace the direct equality check (i == j) with a symbolic equality check using Eq(i, j). When Eq(i, j) clearly evaluates to true, return S.One, and when it is definitively false, return S.Zero. This refactoring will improve the clarity and reliability of the element‐by‐element computation without altering the already correct behavior observed in element-wise and diagonal tests.
feature1.entrypoint: File: sympy/matrices/expressions/matexpr.py; Function: _entry; Focus on the section that evaluates the equality of indices – update the conditional structure to use Eq(i, j).

feature2.prompt: Despite the correct recognition and validation of the identity matrix via element-wise queries and diagonal summation, there is a discrepancy in the overall computation of its total sum. The total sum of the elements is computed as 0 when it is mathematically expected to equal n. This inconsistency highlights a bug in the aggregate operation that totals all the matrix elements. The fix should ensure that when the full double summation is executed, the result correctly returns n, in line with the definition of an identity matrix.
feature2.hint_texts: Within the _entry method in sympy/matrices/expressions/matexpr.py, address the branch that handles cases where the equality between indices cannot be definitively determined. Instead of defaulting to a simplistic outcome, return an expression based on KroneckerDelta to accurately capture the element’s contribution in aggregate operations. This change will directly fix the bug in the overall summation without affecting the individual element evaluations.
feature2.entrypoint: File: sympy/matrices/expressions/matexpr.py; Function: _entry; Focus on the fallback branch where if Eq(i, j) is neither definitively true nor false, the method should return KroneckerDelta(i, j) to ensure the total sum computes correctly.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features involve modifications to the file sympy/matrices/expressions/matexpr.py, particularly the _entry method which is central to the construction of the identity matrix.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: The developers working on feature1 (refactoring internal comparisons) and feature2 (fixing the summation bug) should ensure that their changes are merged in a way that the enhanced equality checking and the corrective use of KroneckerDelta both coexist. A coordinated review of the _entry method is needed so that the improved structure supports the correct total summation.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers must discuss the ordering and integration of changes in the _entry method, ensure that the symbolic equality checks are implemented consistently, and verify that the default handling via KroneckerDelta correctly addresses the summation error. Regular communication is required to avoid conflicts and to validate the combined functionality with integration tests.
